messages.author: b8cd6bb0d7da1036
messages.subject: Why is this model saturated?
parts:
Dear experts,

I have 4 observed variables and I am trying to do some path analyses on them. I started with a saturated model where each pair of variables are linked, and then I removed the paths one by one. And as I expected, the df increased as I removed more paths.

But something bizarre happened when I reach the model shown in the attached figure, since the summary showed that it is saturated again (with 0 df). Could someone explain why it is saturated? And is there a way to easily tell whether a model will be saturated by looking at the path diagram?

Here is the code for specifying the model:

Path_model_5<-'
        level: 1
          epi~a1*exp
          sem~b1*exp
          lifetime~f1*exp 
        level: 2
          epi~a2*exp
          sem~b2*exp
          lifetime~f2*exp'
fit5=sem(Path_model_5,data=data_keep_com,cluster="SSID")


Thanks,
HY

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Why is this model saturated?
parts: Could someone explain why it is saturated?

Because auto.cov.y=TRUE in the sem() function (see ?lavOptions), which applies to "purely" endogenous variables.  I'm guessing in other models, those 3 endogenous variables were also predictors of other variables.
